newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Carlton profit to climb 20 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Carlton profit to climb 20 pct.

text.p: Media group Carlton Communications Plc is expected to announce a rise of around 20 percent in annual pre-tax profit next Wednesday, despite a relatively flat performance from its flagship broadcast television arm.
Analysts are forecasting pre-tax profit of 290-297 million stg for the year to September 30 against a 1995 figure of 246.7 million stg.

Carlton operates the ITV television licences for the English Midlands and London on weekdays. Last weekend it agreed to pay 85 million stg to buy privately-owned Westcountry Television, boosting its total television audience to 22 million people.

Operating profit from broadcast television totalled 122.8 million stg in 1995, 49 percent of the total. However, profit from the division was flat in the first half and analysts expect it to grow by only five percent or so in the full year.

But they are expecting further strong performances from Technicolor, which processes motion picture film, and Quantel, which designs and manufactures image-processing products for the film and television industry worldwide.

Anthony de Larrinaga of Panmure Gordon said he expected Carlton Home Entertainment, part of the Video Production and Distribution division, to cut its losses to around five million stg from 12-13 million last year.
Panmure is forecasting pre-tax profit of 295.6 million stg.
Analysts say that Carlton's balance sheet strength means it is well placed to make further acquisitions in the ITV sector following an easing of ownership restrictions earlier this year.
Some believe it could make a bid for HTV Plc, the broadcaster to Wales and south-west England. HTV sits snugly between Carlton's Central and Westcountry franchises.
However, United News & Media Plc, pipped at the post by Carlton for Westcountry, has recently taken a 20 percent stake in HTV.
